cases.expected: Non‑null TypeValidator instance returned; getValidators() method is invoked exactly once
cases.description: When the internal `validators` field is null, calling `getTypeValidator()` should trigger lazy loading via `getValidators()`. The mocked `getValidators()` populates both `validators` and `typeValidator`. The test verifies that the returned object is not null and that `getValidators()` was called.

cases.expected: The previously set TypeValidator instance is returned; getValidators() is NOT invoked
cases.description: The `validators` list is pre‑populated (e.g., with a dummy validator) and `typeValidator` is set to a known stub. Calling `getTypeValidator()` must return that stub without calling `getValidators()`. The test uses a spy or Mockito `verify` to ensure `getValidators()` is never invoked.

cases.expected: null is returned; getValidators() is invoked but does not set typeValidator
cases.description: Simulate a schema that does not contain a `type` keyword. The mocked `getValidators()` populates `validators` with other validators but leaves `typeValidator` as null. After invoking `getTypeValidator()`, the method should return null, confirming that the lazy‑load path works even when no TypeValidator exists.

cases.expected: First call triggers getValidators(); subsequent calls return the same non‑null TypeValidator instance without invoking getValidators() again
cases.description: Create a JsonSchema spy where getValidators() is stubbed to populate validators and typeValidator. Call getTypeValidator() twice. Verify getValidators() was called exactly once and both returned references are identical.

cases.expected: null is returned; getValidators() is NOT invoked
cases.description: Manually set the `validators` field to an empty ArrayList and leave `typeValidator` as null. Invoke getTypeValidator() and assert that the result is null and that getValidators() was never called.

group: Validators list empty after lazy loading

cases.expected: null is returned; getValidators() is invoked exactly once
cases.description: Mock getValidators() to set `validators` to an empty list and leave `typeValidator` null. Call getTypeValidator() and verify that it returns null while confirming that getValidators() was executed once.

cases.expected: RuntimeException thrown from getValidators() propagates out of getTypeValidator()
cases.description: Configure the JsonSchema spy so that getValidators() throws a RuntimeException (e.g., new IllegalStateException("boom")). Invoke getTypeValidator() and assert that the same exception is thrown to the caller.

cases.expected: Instance of the custom subclass is returned; getValidators() invoked once
cases.description: Create a subclass of TypeValidator (e.g., MySpecialTypeValidator). Stub getValidators() to assign this instance to `typeValidator`. After calling getTypeValidator(), verify that the returned object is an instance of MySpecialTypeValidator and that getValidators() was called exactly once.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown from getValidators() propagates out of getTypeValidator()
cases.description: Configure a JsonSchema spy so that its getValidators() method throws a NullPointerException (e.g., new NullPointerException("null boom")). Invoke getTypeValidator() and assert that the same NullPointerException is thrown to the caller.

cases.expected: AssertionError thrown from getValidators() propagates out of getTypeValidator()
cases.description: Stub getValidators() to throw an AssertionError (or any subclass of java.lang.Error). Call getTypeValidator() and verify that the Error is not caught and propagates unchanged.
